vignette: 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a plantar forefoot ulcer due to diabetic neuropathy, classified Wagner grade III (deep abscess). For the past 6 weeks standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection; serial measurements show no measurable signs of healing over that period. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested as an adjunct, with standard wound care continuing and wound re-evaluation at least every 30 days.
rationale_note: Type 2 DM, Wagner III foot ulcer, 6 weeks of standard care without measurable healing; HBO in chamber adjunctive to ongoing wound care.

vignette: 71-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes and a heel ulcer due to diabetes, classified Wagner grade III. For exactly 30 consecutive days standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection, with weekly measurements showing no measurable signs of healing during those 30 days. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a monoplace chamber is requested, in addition to continued standard wound care, with wound evaluation at least every 30 days.
rationale_note: Boundaries: Wagner grade III exactly; exactly 30 consecutive days without measurable healing.

vignette: 68-year-old woman brought to the emergency department 2 hours after exposure to a malfunctioning furnace, with headache, confusion, and a carboxyhemoglobin level of 28%. She has type 2 diabetes. HBO therapy in a monoplace chamber is requested for acute carbon monoxide intoxication.
rationale_note: Acute CO intoxication in a monoplace (one-man) chamber; diabetic-wound criteria irrelevant.

vignette: 73-year-old man treated with radiation for oropharyngeal cancer 3 years ago, now with osteoradionecrosis of the mandible confirmed on imaging. He is receiving conventional treatment including surgical debridement, antibiotics, and oral care. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested as an adjunct to this conventional treatment.
rationale_note: Osteoradionecrosis as an adjunct to conventional treatment.

vignette: 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a neuropathic plantar ulcer due to diabetes, classified Wagner grade II (deep to tendon, no abscess or osteomyelitis). For 8 weeks standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection, with no measurable signs of healing. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber is requested with continued standard wound care.
rationale_note: Wagner grade II; requires grade III or higher.

vignette: 79-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a stage 4 sacral pressure ulcer after a prolonged hospitalization. The wound has shown no measurable improvement after 10 weeks of debridement, negative-pressure wound therapy, nutrition optimization, glucose control, and pressure off-loading. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested as an adjunct to wound care.
rationale_note: Decubitus (pressure) ulcer is explicitly non-covered, even though the patient has diabetes.

vignette: 70-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a Wagner grade IV forefoot wound due to diabetes. He began adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber 35 days ago after 6 weeks of standard wound care without measurable healing, and standard care has continued. Wound evaluations 30 days apart during HBO show identical wound dimensions and no measurable signs of healing. Continuation of HBO therapy for another 30 days is requested.
rationale_note: No measurable healing during the last 30-day period of HBO; continued treatment is not covered.

vignette: 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a Wagner grade III foot ulcer due to diabetes, discovered 16 days ago. Since then she has had debridement, off-loading, moist dressings, glucose optimization, and treatment of infection. The wound surgeon requests adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber now to accelerate healing, in addition to standard wound care.
rationale_note: Only 2 weeks of standard wound care before HBO; requires >= 30 days without measurable healing.

vignette: 76-year-old man with long-standing peripheral artery disease and chronic ischemic rest pain in the left foot, with no open wound and no acute change. He is not a candidate for revascularization. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested to improve tissue oxygenation for his chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency.
rationale_note: Chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency is explicitly non-covered (acute peripheral arterial insufficiency would be covered).

vignette: 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a plantar foot ulcer due to diabetes measuring 2.5 x 2.0 cm. For 7 weeks standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection, with no measurable signs of healing. The record does not give a Wagner grade or describe wound depth or whether tendon, bone, or abscess is involved. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber is requested with continued standard wound care.
rationale_note: Wound severity not documented; no Wagner grade or depth recorded.

vignette: 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a Wagner grade III ulcer of the lateral foot due to diabetes, which the referral says has been present for 3 months. The record contains no wound care notes, measurements, or description of the standard wound therapy provided during that time. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber is requested.
rationale_note: Wound present for months, but no documentation of the standard wound care given or wound measurements.
